backward_compat_traps.16450_mode: After Master Reset, FCR0=0 (character mode); behaves like 16450.
backward_compat_traps.fifo_mode: Software must explicitly write FCR0=1 to enable FIFOs.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Drivers ported from 16450 silently leave FIFOs disabled; 16550 advantage (reduced CPU interrupts) is not realized.

backward_compat_traps.16550_pins: Pin 24 = TXRDY, Pin 29 = RXRDY (for DMA handshake).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Board designs that relied on CSOUT functionality on pin 24 will fail when populated with 16550 part.

backward_compat_traps.PC16550_1987: Original 16550 had an RX FIFO error that lost characters under certain conditions; not safe to enable FIFOs.
backward_compat_traps.PC16550A_and_later: FIFOs are functional; software typically checks IIR bits 7-6 to detect a 'usable FIFO' part.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Defensive drivers check FIFO-detection signature (write FCR, read back IIR) before enabling FIFO mode.
Forgetting to clear DLAB after setting baud rate causes subsequent THR writes to corrupt the divisor latch.

lineage.summary: Original IBM PC serial-port UART; no FIFOs.
Faster INS8250; no FIFOs; widely used in IBM PC/AT.
First version with 16-byte FIFOs; had RX FIFO bug.
FIFO bug fixed; widely deployed in 286/386 era.
Current National Semiconductor part; M2CMOS process; 24 MHz max XIN.

fields.version_naming_history_note: The LIN Consortium released seven revisions (1.0 → 1.1 → 1.2 → 1.3 → 2.0 → 2.1 → 2.2 → 2.2A) between 1999 and 2010. LIN 2.0 was the major revision step that standardised diagnostics, configuration, and the Node Capability File workflow. LIN 2.2A is the final revision before the LIN protocol was harmonised into ISO 17987 (2016+).
previous_versions: CAN 1.2 — Bosch CAN spec used through late 1980s; standard 11-bit identifier format only.
CAN 2.0 Part A — message format equivalent to CAN 1.2.
CAN 2.0 Part B — adds 29-bit extended identifier format; standard + extended messages coexist on same network.

key_changes.summary: Renamed/clarified CAN 1.2 11-bit identifier format; introduced four frame types (DATA / REMOTE / ERROR / OVERLOAD); fault confinement formalized.
Adds 29-bit extended identifier format; backward-compatible with Part A nodes provided extended-format messages are not used in mixed networks.
Upwards-compatible modifications increase max oscillator tolerance from 0.5 % to 1.5 % by allowing SOF at the 3rd INTERMISSION bit etc.
